comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C5, C37-C40. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers support the finding that IL-25R-deficient mice fail to expel parasites in the chronic phase (day 28) but not acute phase (day 14). No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Perfect agreement on claims C41-C43, C47-C48, C108. Both evaluations support that adaptive Th2 responses develop normally in IL-25R-deficient mice, establishing that IL-25R is not required for adaptive immunity. This finding is accepted as a key distinction between adaptive and innate effector mechanisms.

Perfect agreement on claims C44-C46, C109. Both evaluations support the finding that eosinophil and macrophage responses are impaired in IL-25R-deficient mice. OpenEval notes the temporal dynamics and partial recovery require clarification, but peer reviewers raised no concerns about these measurements.

Strong agreement on claims C56-C57, C116 regarding bone marrow chimera experiments showing IL-25R is required on hematopoietic cells. OpenEval notes missing chimerism efficiency data, but peer reviewers accepted the findings without raising this concern.

Both address temporal IL-25 effects (C6, C32, C73-C77). OpenEval supports that late but not early IL-25 drives expulsion. Peer reviewers accepted the timing experiments showing IL-25 stimulates late clearance. Strong agreement on the temporal requirement for IL-25 in the effector phase.

Both address IL-25 and IL-4 synergy (C58-C61). OpenEval supports the synergistic effects in Rag1-/- mice but questions whether synergy is truly mechanistic versus additive. Peer reviewers found the IL-4/IL-25 data interesting and raised no concerns about the synergy findings.

Both address claims C78-C82 regarding cellular responses to late IL-25. OpenEval supports that late IL-25 does not broadly activate lymphoid responses and that ILC2s remain a small fraction. However, peer reviewers note uncertainty, stating 'Figure 4H is supportive of IL-25 up-regulating ILC2 and this correlates with protection,' creating tension with the ILC-independence conclusion.

Major disagreement on claims C69-C72, C118, C139 regarding ILC dispensability. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to incomplete depletion and methodological limitations. Peer reviewers rate as UNSUPPORTED, stating the conclusion 'may be premature' and noting that inflammatory ILC2s express low CD90 and may not be efficiently depleted. Peer reviewers request additional experiments in RAG γc chain null mice for definitive testing.

Strong agreement on claims C89-C93, C125-C126 showing IL-25 activates macrophages and eosinophils to produce IL-13. Both evaluations support these findings as key cellular targets of IL-25. OpenEval notes statistical significance; peer reviewers acknowledged the data positively.

Perfect agreement on claims C94-C96, C130 regarding in vitro IL-25/IL-4 synergy on macrophages. Both evaluations support the synergy findings. OpenEval notes lack of mechanistic insight and supraphysiological concentrations, but peer reviewers raised no such concerns.

Perfect agreement on claims C98-C103, C131 showing IL-4Rα is required for IL-25 effects. Both evaluations support this hierarchical relationship between IL-4Rα and IL-25R signaling. OpenEval notes uncertainty about cell-intrinsic versus indirect requirements, but peer reviewers accepted the findings.

Partial agreement on main conclusions (C9, C107, C110, C129, C137, C140). OpenEval supports the overall model but notes C137 (macrophage IL-13 drives epithelial expulsion) is inferred rather than directly demonstrated. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, accepting the IL-25/IL-4 synergy findings but challenging the ILC-independence claim as potentially premature, requesting either additional experiments or revision of the major conclusion.
OpenEval evaluated background/literature claims C1-C36 as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background statements.

OpenEval evaluated discussion claims C49-C133 (selected) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations, noting some speculative interpretations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these discussion points.
OpenEval evaluated claims C3-C4, C97 describing the H. polygyrus model system as SUPPORTED based on established literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval rated claims C127, C138 as UNCERTAIN, noting that macrophages being the 'major' source of IL-13 is not quantitatively demonstrated compared to other cellular sources. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific quantitative concern.
